lines.text: This is Jig. Describe the app you need, and Meta's Muse Spark builds it: a native app, on iPhone and Android at once.
The model writes the app as a spec. Jig validates it and renders every screen, and when something fails, the model repairs it on its own.
It runs natively. UIKit on the left, Android Views on the right, from the same spec.
When a plant is due, it shows up here, and Jig schedules a nine a.m. reminder that fires even while the app is closed.
To change something, select it and say what you want. The model edits just that part, then checks a screenshot of its work.
Apps can share data, with your permission. Here's a shopping list that reads the pantry app.
This time the model also writes a small script to merge the lists, and Jig runs it in a sandbox. Every app gets storage, reminders and a shared data store for free.
Jig asks once before one app reads another's data. Low items come straight from the pantry, and you can add your own.
Now the pantry runs low on jars...
and the list picks it up.
Apps can use Meta's model too. A dinner planner: type what's in your fridge, and get three quick recipes.
The app asks Meta's model through the shell, so your API key never reaches the app.
Save the ones you like. Describe it, use it, change it. That's Jig.
